how_you_can_help: Support whale-safe shipping policies, donate to ocean noise-reduction campaigns, and choose sustainably sourced seafood to reduce entanglement risks.
fun_fact: Blue whales can produce sounds louder than a jet engine — up to 188 decibels — heard across entire ocean basins.

how_you_can_help: Never buy products made from tortoiseshell, support marine protected areas, and volunteer with sea turtle nesting-beach patrols.
fun_fact: Hawksbill turtles are one of the few animals that can eat toxic sea sponges that other species avoid.

how_you_can_help: Refuse to buy shrimp and fish caught with gillnets in the Upper Gulf of California, and support organizations pushing for a permanent gillnet ban.
fun_fact: The vaquita was only discovered in 1958 and may be extinct within this decade.

how_you_can_help: Reduce boat speeds in seagrass habitats, support seagrass restoration projects, and report illegal dugong hunting to local authorities.
fun_fact: Dugongs can live over 70 years and are thought to be the origin of ancient mermaid legends.

how_you_can_help: Never consume shark fin soup, support sustainable fishing certifications, and practice responsible snorkelling and diving around whale sharks.
fun_fact: Whale sharks are filter feeders that can live over 100 years and are the world's largest fish.

how_you_can_help: Advocate for shark-finning bans, support catch-and-release fishing for sharks, and choose MSC-certified seafood.
fun_fact: Great hammerheads use their oddly shaped heads like a metal detector to find stingrays buried in sand.

how_you_can_help: Reduce plastic use (especially bags and balloons that resemble jellyfish), support beach clean-ups, and back climate-action initiatives.
fun_fact: Leatherbacks can dive deeper than 1,200 m and travel over 10,000 km on a single migration.

how_you_can_help: Reduce your carbon footprint to slow Arctic ice loss, support Indigenous-led conservation programs, and avoid products linked to Arctic drilling.
fun_fact: Narwhals' spiral tusks are actually teeth — they can grow up to 3 metres long.

how_you_can_help: Avoid tours that chase or crowd dolphins, support community-based river conservation, and reduce plastic waste entering waterways.
fun_fact: Irrawaddy dolphins cooperate with fishermen, herding fish into nets in exchange for a share of the catch.

how_you_can_help: Demand shark-finning bans from lawmakers, avoid unsustainably caught tuna, and support marine sanctuaries in the open ocean.
fun_fact: Oceanic whitetip sharks were once described as the most abundant large animal on Earth. Now they're critically endangered.

how_you_can_help: Support the IWC commercial-whaling moratorium, reduce ocean noise pollution awareness, and donate to whale research organizations.
fun_fact: Sei whales are among the fastest cetaceans, capable of bursts up to 50 km/h.

how_you_can_help: Reduce single-use plastics, volunteer for beach clean-ups during nesting season, and turn off beachfront lights at night to protect hatchlings.
fun_fact: Green turtles navigate thousands of kilometres to lay eggs on the exact beach where they were born.

how_you_can_help: Choose reef-safe sunscreen, never buy humphead wrasse at restaurants, and support marine park enforcement in coral reef regions.
fun_fact: Humphead wrasse can live 30+ years and change sex from female to male as they age.

how_you_can_help: Choose pole-and-line or troll-caught fish, push for international catch limits on mako sharks, and support tagging and research programs.
fun_fact: Shortfin mako sharks can leap up to 6 metres out of the water when hooked.

how_you_can_help: Use reef-safe sunscreen, reduce carbon emissions to fight ocean warming, and support coral reef restoration and nursery projects.
fun_fact: A single staghorn coral colony can grow several centimetres per year — but bleaching can kill it overnight.
